STROBE: Item
Recommendation (STROBE, cohort studies)
Reported in
Title and abstract 1(a)
Indicate the study's design with a commonly used term in the title or the abstract
Title ('audit'); Methods, 'Design, terminology and estimable quantities'; Abstract, Methods
Title and abstract 1(b)
Provide in the abstract an informative and balanced summary of what was done and what was found
Abstract (Objectives, Methods, Results, Conclusion); Key Points
Introduction — Background/rationale 2
Explain the scientific background and rationale for the investigation being reported
Introduction, paragraphs 1–3
Introduction — Objectives 3
State specific objectives, including any prespecified hypotheses
Introduction, final paragraph; Abstract, Objectives
Methods — Study design 4
Present key elements of study design early in the paper
Methods, 'Design, terminology and estimable quantities'
Methods — Setting 5
Describe the setting, locations, and relevant dates, including periods of recruitment, exposure, follow-up, and data collection
Methods, 'Participants, reference standard and index tests' (single tertiary children's hospital, December 2012–June 2026)
Methods — Participants 6(a)
Give the eligibility criteria, and the sources and methods of selection of participants
Methods, 'Participants…' (consecutive children with an operative diagnosis of malrotation; institutional clinical and surgical records database)
Methods — Participants 6(b)
For matched studies, give matching criteria and number of exposed and unexposed
Not applicable (no matching)
Methods — Variables 7
Clearly define all outcomes, exposures, predictors, potential confounders, and effect modifiers. Give diagnostic criteria, if applicable

Methods, 'Design, terminology…' (report-level detection defined); 'Participants…' (volvulus definition); 'Report-content audit and classification' (positivity criteria, content items); Online Resource 1
Methods — Data sources/measurement 8
For each variable of interest, give sources of data and details of methods of assessment. Describe comparability of assessment methods if there is more than one group
Methods, 'Report-content audit and classification'; Online Resource 1, Sections A–J
Methods — Bias 9
Describe any efforts to address potential sources of bias

Methods, 'Design, terminology…' (three stated consequences of the case-only design); Discussion, paragraph on incorporation bias, pathway position and confounding by indication; Table 1 displays confounding by indication rather than adjusting it
Methods — Study size 10
Explain how the study size was arrived at
Methods, 'Participants…' (all consecutive eligible children; no sample-size calculation)
Methods — Quantitative variables 11
Explain how quantitative variables were handled in the analyses; if applicable, describe which groupings were chosen and why
Methods, 'Statistical analysis' (age category ≤28 days / 29 days–1 year / >1 year; era 2012–2018 vs 2019–2026); certainty tiers in 'Report-content audit and classification'
Methods — Statistical methods 12(a)
Describe all statistical methods, including those used to control for confounding
Methods, 'Statistical analysis' (GEE with patient-level clustering; adjustment for era and age category)
Methods — Statistical methods 12(b)
Describe any methods used to examine subgroups and interactions
Methods, 'Statistical analysis' (modality-by-volvulus interaction, non-estimable owing to complete separation; subgroup receiving all three modalities); Online Resource 2
Methods — Statistical methods 12(c)
Explain how missing data were addressed
Results, 'Cohort…' (the 55 children without an index test characterised, not imputed); Discussion, Limitations (informative missingness)
Methods — Statistical methods 12(d)
If applicable, explain how loss to follow-up was addressed
Not applicable (no follow-up; single preoperative index test per modality)
Methods — Statistical methods 12(e)
Describe any sensitivity analyses
Methods, 'Statistical analysis' and 'Report-content audit and classification' (reclassification of possible-tier conclusions; paired analysis restricted to 48 h and 24 h); Online Resource 2
Results — Participants 13(a)
Report numbers of individuals at each stage of study
Results, 'Cohort…'; Fig. 1
Results — Participants 13(b)
Give reasons for non-participation at each stage
Results, 'Cohort…' (the 55 children without an index test, with the imaging they did receive); Fig. 1
Results — Participants 13(c)
Consider use of a flow diagram
Fig. 1
Results — Descriptive data 14(a)
Give characteristics of study participants and information on exposures and potential confounders
Table 1 (overall and by index test received)
Results — Descriptive data 14(b)
Indicate number of participants with missing data for each variable of interest
Results, 'Cohort…'; Table 1 footnote; denominators shown with every rate
Results — Descriptive data 14(c)
Summarise follow-up time
Not applicable
Results — Outcome data 15
Report numbers of outcome events or summary measures over time
Table 2 (detection with denominators); Table 3 (ultrasound report content); Table 4 (change between eras)
Results — Main results 16(a)
Give unadjusted estimates and, if applicable, confounder-adjusted estimates and their precision. Make clear which confounders were adjusted for and why they were included
Results, 'Detection and certainty of wording' (unadjusted and adjusted GEE odds ratios); Online Resource 2, Table S3
Results — Main results 16(b)
Report category boundaries when continuous variables were categorized
Methods, 'Statistical analysis'; Online Resource 2, Table S5
Results — Main results 16(c)
If relevant, consider translating estimates of relative risk into absolute risk for a meaningful time period
Detection rates are reported as absolute proportions with denominators throughout (Table 2, Figs 2–3)
Results — Other analyses 17
Report other analyses done — eg analyses of subgroups and interactions, and sensitivity analyses
Results, 'Documented content of ultrasound examinations', 'Change in detection over time', 'Selected subgroup and populations not represented'; Online Resources 2 and 3
Discussion — Key results 18
Summarise key results with reference to study objectives
Discussion, paragraphs 1–3; Conclusion
Discussion — Limitations 19
Discuss limitations of the study, taking into account sources of potential bias or imprecision. Discuss both direction and magnitude of any potential bias
Discussion, 'Limitations'; and the paragraph on incorporation bias, pathway position and confounding by indication, which states the direction of each
Discussion — Interpretation 20
Give a cautious overall interpretation of results considering objectives, limitations, multiplicity of analyses, results from similar studies, and other relevant evidence
Discussion, paragraphs 2–5; Conclusion (explicit statement that no sensitivity, specificity or ranking is established)
Discussion — Generalisability 21
Discuss the generalisability (external validity) of the study results
Results, 'Selected subgroup and populations not represented'; Discussion, Limitations (single centre; skew toward severe neonatal disease)
Other information — Funding 22
Give the source of funding and the role of the funders for the present study and, if applicable, for the original study on which the present article is based
Declarations, Funding (and title page)
